subproblem.title: normDet of a block lower-triangular map between Euclidean products
subproblem.statement:
Let E₁, E₂, F₁, F₂ be finite-dimensional real inner product spaces (in Type) with dim E₁ = dim F₁ and dim E₂ = dim F₂.
Give WithLp 2 (E₁ × E₂) and WithLp 2 (F₁ × F₂) their Euclidean (L²) product inner products, ⟨(u,v),(u',v')⟩ = ⟨u,u'⟩ + ⟨v,v'⟩. Their components are WithLp.fst and WithLp.snd.
Let G : WithLp 2 (E₁ × E₂) → WithLp 2 (F₁ × F₂), G₁₁ : E₁ → F₁ and G₂₂ : E₂ → F₂ be ℝ-linear maps such that:
(i) WithLp.fst(G(toLp(0, b))) = 0 for all b ∈ E₂;
(ii) G₁₁ a = WithLp.fst(G(toLp(a, 0))) for all a ∈ E₁;
(iii) G₂₂ b = WithLp.snd(G(toLp(0, b))) for all b ∈ E₂.
Then normDet(G) = normDet(G₁₁) · normDet(G₂₂), where normDet is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (E₁ E₂ F₁ F₂ : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E₁] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E₁] [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E₂] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E₂] [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F₁] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F₁] [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F₂] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F₂] (G : WithLp 2 (E₁ × E₂) →ₗ[ℝ] WithLp 2 (F₁ × F₂)) (G₁₁ : E₁ →ₗ[ℝ] F₁) (G₂₂ : E₂ →ₗ[ℝ] F₂), Module.finrank ℝ E₁ = Module.finrank ℝ F₁ → Module.finrank ℝ E₂ = Module.finrank ℝ F₂ → (∀ b : E₂, WithLp.fst (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (0, b))) = 0) → (∀ a : E₁, G₁₁ a = WithLp.fst (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (a, 0)))) → (∀ b : E₂, G₂₂ b = WithLp.snd (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (0, b)))) → G.normDet = G₁₁.normDet * G₂₂.normDet
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 of the parent proof, stated abstractly for maps between L²-products. There, in orthonormal bases adapted to P₁ ⊕ P₂ and Q^⊥ ⊕ Q, the matrix of Ã is the block lower-triangular matrix [[α, 0], [β, Θ₂]], hence |det Ã| = |det α|·|det Θ₂|.

Setup and conventions.
- E₁, E₂, F₁, F₂ are finite-dimensional real inner product spaces with d₁ := dim E₁ = dim F₁ and d₂ := dim E₂ = dim F₂.
- On WithLp 2 (X × Y) the inner product is ⟨w, w'⟩ = ⟨w₁, w'₁⟩ + ⟨w₂, w'₂⟩, where w₁ = WithLp.fst w and w₂ = WithLp.snd w (Mathlib WithLp.prod_inner_apply; the instance is WithLp.instProdInnerProductSpace).
- Hypotheses: (H0) (G(toLp(0,b)))₁ = 0 for all b ∈ E₂; (H11) G₁₁ a = (G(toLp(a,0)))₁ for all a ∈ E₁; (H22) G₂₂ b = (G(toLp(0,b)))₂ for all b ∈ E₂.

Fact used (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_eq_norm_det_toMatrix). Let f : U → V be linear between finite-dimensional inner product spaces, and let u, v be orthonormal bases of U and V indexed by the same finite type. Then normDet f = |det 𝔐|, where 𝔐 is the matrix of f in (u, v).

1. Orthonormal bases. Let e¹ be an orthonormal basis of E₁ indexed by Fin d₁ (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E₁). Let f¹ be an orthonormal basis of F₁ indexed by Fin d₁: stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ F₁ is indexed by Fin (dim F₁), so reindex it along dim F₁ = d₁. Similarly take e² of E₂ and f² of F₂, indexed by Fin d₂.

2. Product bases. Let e := e¹.prod e² and f := f¹.prod f² (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.prod). They are orthonormal bases of WithLp 2 (E₁ × E₂) and WithLp 2 (F₁ × F₂), indexed by Fin d₁ ⊕ Fin d₂, with e(inl i) = toLp(e¹ᵢ, 0) and e(inr j) = toLp(0, e²ⱼ), and similarly for f. Orthonormality follows from the sum formula for the inner product.

3. Coordinates in f. Let w ∈ WithLp 2 (F₁ × F₂).
   - The coordinate of w along f(inl i) is ⟨f(inl i), w⟩ = ⟨f¹ᵢ, w₁⟩ + ⟨0, w₂⟩ = ⟨f¹ᵢ, w₁⟩, i.e. the i-th coordinate of w₁ in f¹.
   - Similarly, the coordinate along f(inr j) is the j-th coordinate of w₂ in f².
   (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply and prod_apply.)

4. The matrix of G. Let 𝔊 be the matrix of G in (e, f), so 𝔊(r, s) is the coordinate of G(e s) along f r. Its four blocks are:
   (a) r = inl i, s = inl j: the i-th f¹-coordinate of (G(toLp(e¹ⱼ, 0)))₁ = G₁₁ e¹ⱼ (by H11). This is entry (i, j) of the matrix 𝔄 of G₁₁ in (e¹, f¹).
   (b) r = inl i, s = inr j: the i-th f¹-coordinate of (G(toLp(0, e²ⱼ)))₁ = 0 (by H0). So this block is 0.
   (c) r = inr i, s = inl j: the i-th f²-coordinate of (G(toLp(e¹ⱼ, 0)))₂. Call this matrix 𝔆; no hypothesis is needed on it.
   (d) r = inr i, s = inr j: the i-th f²-coordinate of (G(toLp(0, e²ⱼ)))₂ = G₂₂ e²ⱼ (by H22). This is entry (i, j) of the matrix 𝔇 of G₂₂ in (e², f²).
   Hence 𝔊 = fromBlocks 𝔄 0 𝔆 𝔇, a block lower-triangular matrix with square diagonal blocks (d₁×d₁ and d₂×d₂).

5. Block determinant: det(fromBlocks 𝔄 0 𝔆 𝔇) = det 𝔄 · det 𝔇 (Mathlib Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₁₂; this is the standard determinant of a block-triangular matrix).

6. By the Fact, applied three times with index types Fin d₁ ⊕ Fin d₂, Fin d₁ and Fin d₂: normDet G = |det 𝔊|, normDet G₁₁ = |det 𝔄| and normDet G₂₂ = |det 𝔇|. Therefore normDet G = |det 𝔄 · det 𝔇| = |det 𝔄| · |det 𝔇| = normDet G₁₁ · normDet G₂₂. ∎

Degenerate cases. If d₁ = 0 or d₂ = 0, the corresponding blocks are empty and have determinant 1; the argument is unchanged. The equal-dimension hypotheses are exactly what makes the diagonal blocks square.

  classical
  let bE₁ := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E₁
  let bE₂ := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E₂
  let bF₁ := (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ F₁).reindex (finCongr h₁.symm)
  let bF₂ := (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ F₂).reindex (finCongr h₂.symm)

  let bF := bF₁.prod bF₂

    intro v i
    simp [bF, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply]
  have hrepr₂ : ∀ (v : WithLp 2 (F₁ × F₂)) i, bF.repr v (Sum.inr i) = bF₂.repr (WithLp.snd v) i := by
    intro v i
    simp [bF, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply]
  have hmat : LinearMap.toMatrix bE.toBasis bF.toBasis G =

    · simp [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, hrepr₂, bE]
    · simp [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, hrepr₂, bE, hG₂₂]

subproblem.title: The co-area Jacobian is the norm determinant of the adjoint of df_x restricted to T_x M
subproblem.statement:
Let N, m ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ and x ∈ ℝᴺ, where ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
Put T := tangentSpace M x. It is a linear subspace of ℝᴺ, finite-dimensional, with the restricted inner product.
Let L := (fderiv ℝ f x) ∘ ι : T → ℝᵐ, where ι : T → ℝᴺ is the inclusion. In Lean, L = ((fderiv ℝ f x).comp (tangentSpace M x).subtypeL).toLinearMap.
Let L* := LinearMap.adjoint L : ℝᵐ → T.
Then coareaJacobian M f x = normDet(L*), where normDet is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N m : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (x : Rn N), coareaJacobian M f x = (LinearMap.adjoint ((fderiv ℝ f x).comp (tangentSpace M x).subtypeL).toLinearMap).normDet
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's Notation paragraph ("Unfolding the definition ... coareaJacobian M f x = Real.sqrt(det(L ∘ L*))") and its listed normDet facts. Also the parentheticals of parent Steps 2 and 8 (SimonGMT coareaLinearJacobian_eq_sqrt_det). This is the identity √det(LL*) = normDet(L*), which both parts of the parent use.

Notation. Fix N, m, M, f, x.
- T := tangentSpace M x, a linear subspace of the finite-dimensional space ℝᴺ with the restricted inner product. T is finite-dimensional, hence complete; so is ℝᵐ.
- ι := T.subtypeL : T → ℝᴺ, the inclusion; D := fderiv ℝ f x.
- Lc := D ∘L ι : T →L[ℝ] ℝᵐ and L := Lc.toLinearMap : T →ₗ[ℝ] ℝᵐ.
- g := L* := LinearMap.adjoint L : ℝᵐ →ₗ[ℝ] T.
The right-hand side of the claim is normDet(g).

1. By definition, coareaJacobian M f x = Real.sqrt((Lc ∘L Lc†).det), where Lc† := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint Lc. The let-binding in the definition is definitional.

2. ContinuousLinearMap.det is an abbreviation for LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map. The underlying linear map of Lc ∘L Lc† is L ∘ₗ (Lc†).toLinearMap. In finite dimensions (Lc†).toLinearMap = LinearMap.adjoint L = g (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_toLinearMap, true by rfl). Hence coareaJacobian M f x = Real.sqrt(det(L ∘ₗ g)).

3. Apply Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq to g : ℝᵐ → T (finite-dimensional domain and codomain): (normDet g)² = det(g* ∘ₗ g). For 𝕜 = ℝ the coercion ℝ → 𝕜 is the identity. The adjoint is involutive (LinearMap.adjoint_adjoint), so g* = L and (normDet g)² = det(L ∘ₗ g).

4. normDet g ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg), so Real.sqrt((normDet g)²) = normDet g (Real.sqrt_sq).

5. By steps 2, 3 and 4: coareaJacobian M f x = Real.sqrt(det(L ∘ₗ g)) = Real.sqrt((normDet g)²) = normDet g = normDet(LinearMap.adjoint L). ∎

No case distinction is needed. If m = 0, both sides equal 1: g is a map out of the zero space, so normDet g = 1, and L ∘ₗ g is the identity of the zero space, with determinant 1. Steps 1–5 cover this case verbatim.

theorem Submission.coareaJacobian_eq_normDet_adjoint : (∀ (N m : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (x : Rn N), coareaJacobian M f x = (LinearMap.adjoint ((fderiv ℝ f x).comp (tangentSpace M x).subtypeL).toLinearMap).normDet) := by
  intro N m M f x
  set L : tangentSpace M x →L[ℝ] Rn m := (fderiv ℝ f x).comp (tangentSpace M x).subtypeL with hL
  have hsq := (LinearMap.adjoint L.toLinearMap).normDet_sq
  rw [LinearMap.adjoint_adjoint] at hsq
  have hnn := (LinearMap.adjoint L.toLinearMap).normDet_nonneg
  unfold coareaJacobian
  simp only at hsq ⊢
  rw [← Real.sqrt_sq hnn]
  congr 1
  exact (hsq.trans rfl).symm
proof_key_steps: Unfold coareaJacobian. ContinuousLinearMap.det is LinearMap.det of the underlying map, and (Lc†).toLinearMap = LinearMap.adjoint L (rfl), so coareaJacobian M f x = √det(L ∘ₗ L*).
LinearMap.normDet_sq for g = L* gives (normDet g)² = det(g* ∘ₗ g) = det(L ∘ₗ L*), using adjoint_adjoint.
normDet g ≥ 0, so √((normDet g)²) = normDet g. Hence coareaJacobian M f x = normDet(L*).

subproblem.title: Lemma L: normDet(L*) · normDet(Φ) = normDet(Φ ∘ (0,·)) for a chart Φ straightening L
subproblem.statement:
Let m, k ∈ ℕ and let T be a finite-dimensional real inner product space (in Type).
Let P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ) be the Euclidean product, with first component p₁ = WithLp.fst p.
Let L : T → ℝᵐ, Φ : P → T and Ψ : ℝᵏ → T be ℝ-linear maps such that:
- Φ is bijective;
- L(Φ p) = p₁ for all p ∈ P;
- Ψ b = Φ(toLp(0, b)) for all b ∈ ℝᵏ.
Then normDet(L*) · normDet(Φ) = normDet(Ψ), where L* = LinearMap.adjoint L : ℝᵐ → T and normDet is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ) (T : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup T] [InnerProductSpace ℝ T] [FiniteDimensional ℝ T] (L : T →ₗ[ℝ] Rn m) (Φ : WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) →ₗ[ℝ] T) (Ψ : Rn k →ₗ[ℝ] T), Function.Bijective Φ → (∀ p, L (Φ p) = WithLp.fst p) → (∀ b, Ψ b = Φ (WithLp.toLp 2 (0, b))) → (LinearMap.adjoint L).normDet * Φ.normDet = Ψ.normDet
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 4–9 of the parent proof (Lemma L), with T = tangentSpace M x abstracted to an arbitrary finite-dimensional inner product space T. The isomorphism Ã becomes the bijection Φ and Θ₂ becomes Ψ. The block computation of parent Step 6 is the sibling lemma block_triangular_normdet.

Setup. P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ), with inner product ⟨p, p'⟩ = ⟨p₁, p'₁⟩ + ⟨p₂, p'₂⟩, where p₁ = WithLp.fst p and p₂ = WithLp.snd p. Hypotheses: (Hbij) Φ is bijective; (HL) L(Φ p) = p₁ for all p; (HΨ) Ψ b = Φ(toLp(0, b)) for all b.

1. L is surjective: for a ∈ ℝᵐ, L(Φ(toLp(a, 0))) = (toLp(a, 0))₁ = a by (HL).

2. Dimensions.
   - P ≅ ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ linearly (WithLp.linearEquiv), and dim ℝⁿ = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), so dim P = m + k.
   - Φ is a linear isomorphism (LinearEquiv.ofBijective), so dim T = m + k.
   - Let Q := ker L ⊆ T and let Q^⊥ be its orthogonal complement in T. By rank–nullity and step 1 (range L = ℝᵐ), dim Q = (m + k) − m = k. This is SimonGMT Chapter02.coarea_kernel_finrank, or LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker.
   - Since dim Q + dim Q^⊥ = dim T (Submodule.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal), dim Q^⊥ = m.

3. Orthogonal coordinates. Let π₁ : T → Q^⊥ and π₂ : T → Q be the orthogonal projections (Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto). Then t = π₁ t + π₂ t, and C : T → WithLp 2 (Q^⊥ × Q), C t := toLp(π₁ t, π₂ t), is a linear isometric equivalence (by Pythagoras). In Lean one may take C := SimonGMT Chapter02.coareaCoordinates L, i.e. (ker L).orthogonalDecomposition followed by LinearIsometryEquiv.withLpProdComm. Its value is toLp(π₁ t, π₂ t), by simp with Submodule.orthogonalDecomposition_apply and LinearIsometryEquiv.withLpProdComm_apply.

4. Let G := C ∘ Φ : P → WithLp 2 (Q^⊥ × Q). Since dim P = dim T, normDet(G) = normDet(C) · normDet(Φ) (LinearMap.normDet_comp_of_finrank_eq). normDet(C) = 1 because C is a linear isometry (LinearIsometry.normDet_eq_one). Hence normDet G = normDet Φ.

5. Ψ maps into Q: L(Ψ b) = L(Φ(toLp(0, b))) = (toLp(0, b))₁ = 0. Consequently, for every b ∈ ℝᵏ:
   - (G(toLp(0, b)))₁ = π₁(Φ(toLp(0, b))) = π₁(Ψ b) = 0, because Ψ b ∈ Q ⊆ (Q^⊥)^⊥ (Submodule.le_orthogonal_orthogonal, Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_apply_of_mem_orthogonal);
   - (G(toLp(0, b)))₂ = π₂(Ψ b) = Ψ b (Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_mem_subspace_eq_self).

6. Define linear maps α : ℝᵐ → Q^⊥, α a := (G(toLp(a, 0)))₁ = π₁(Φ(toLp(a, 0))), and Θ : ℝᵏ → Q, Θ b := (G(toLp(0, b)))₂. They are linear as compositions of G with the linear embeddings a ↦ toLp(a, 0), b ↦ toLp(0, b) and the coordinate maps WithLp.fstL, WithLp.sndL. By step 5, Θ b = Ψ b for all b, i.e. Θ = Ψ.codRestrict Q. Following a map by the isometric inclusion of a subspace does not change normDet (LinearMap.normDet_codRestrict), so normDet Θ = normDet Ψ.

7. Apply the sibling lemma block_triangular_normdet (Submission.coarea_normDet_block_triangular) with E₁ := ℝᵐ, E₂ := ℝᵏ, F₁ := Q^⊥, F₂ := Q, the map G, G₁₁ := α and G₂₂ := Θ. Its hypotheses hold:
   - dim ℝᵐ = m = dim Q^⊥ and dim ℝᵏ = k = dim Q (step 2);
   - (G(toLp(0, b)))₁ = 0 (step 5);
   - α and Θ satisfy their defining equations by construction (step 6).
   Hence normDet G = normDet α · normDet Θ. With steps 4 and 6: normDet Φ = normDet α · normDet Ψ.

8. Let λ := L|_{Q^⊥} : Q^⊥ → ℝᵐ (SimonGMT Chapter02.coareaHorizontalLinear L = L.domRestrict (ker L)ᗮ). For t ∈ T, π₂ t ∈ Q = ker L, so λ(π₁ t) = L(π₁ t) = L(t − π₂ t) = L t (SimonGMT Chapter02.coareaHorizontalLinear_coordinates). Taking t := Φ(toLp(a, 0)) gives λ(α a) = L(Φ(toLp(a, 0))) = a by (HL), so λ ∘ α = id on ℝᵐ. Since dim ℝᵐ = m = dim Q^⊥, normDet(λ ∘ α) = normDet λ · normDet α (LinearMap.normDet_comp_of_finrank_eq), and normDet(id) = 1 (LinearMap.normDet_id). Therefore normDet λ · normDet α = 1.

9. normDet λ = normDet(L*). This is SimonGMT Chapter02.coareaHorizontalLinear_normDet for surjective L (step 1): its statement is (coareaHorizontalLinear L).normDet = coareaLinearJacobian L, and coareaLinearJacobian L := L.adjoint.normDet by definition. A self-contained proof:
   (i) range L* = (ker L)^⊥ = Q^⊥ (LinearMap.orthogonal_ker). So κ := L*.codRestrict Q^⊥ : ℝᵐ → Q^⊥ is defined, and normDet κ = normDet L* (normDet_codRestrict).
   (ii) For y ∈ ℝᵐ and q ∈ Q^⊥: ⟨κ y, q⟩ = ⟨L* y, q⟩ = ⟨y, L q⟩ = ⟨y, λ q⟩. Hence κ = λ* (LinearMap.eq_adjoint_iff).
   (iii) λ maps between two spaces of dimension m. In orthonormal bases with a common index type, the matrix of λ* is the transpose of the matrix Λ of λ (LinearMap.toMatrix_adjoint). So normDet λ* = |det Λᵀ| = |det Λ| = normDet λ (normDet_eq_norm_det_toMatrix; this is SimonGMT normDet_adjoint_of_finrank_eq).
   Thus normDet L* = normDet κ = normDet λ* = normDet λ.

10. Conclusion: normDet(L*) · normDet(Φ) = normDet λ · (normDet α · normDet Ψ) = (normDet λ · normDet α) · normDet Ψ = 1 · normDet Ψ = normDet Ψ. ∎

Degenerate cases.
- m = 0: Q^⊥ = 0, and α, λ are maps between zero spaces with normDet 1.
- k = 0: Q = 0, and Θ, Ψ are maps out of the zero space with normDet 1.
All steps hold verbatim; the block lemma has no positivity requirement on the dimensions.

theorem Submission.coarea_normDet_adjoint_mul_normDet_chart : (∀ (m k : ℕ) (T : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup T] [InnerProductSpace ℝ T] [FiniteDimensional ℝ T] (L : T →ₗ[ℝ] Rn m) (Φ : WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) →ₗ[ℝ] T) (Ψ : Rn k →ₗ[ℝ] T), Function.Bijective Φ → (∀ p, L (Φ p) = WithLp.fst p) → (∀ b, Ψ b = Φ (WithLp.toLp 2 (0, b))) → (LinearMap.adjoint L).normDet * Φ.normDet = Ψ.normDet) := by
  intro m k T _ _ _ L Φ Ψ hΦ hL hΨ
  have hsurj : Function.Surjective L := fun a => ⟨Φ (WithLp.toLp 2 (a, 0)), by rw [hL]; rfl⟩
  have hP : Module.finrank ℝ (WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k)) = m + k := by
    rw [(WithLp.linearEquiv 2 ℝ (Rn m × Rn k)).finrank_eq, Module.finrank_prod]
    simp
  have hT : Module.finrank ℝ T = m + k := by
    rw [← (LinearEquiv.ofBijective Φ hΦ).finrank_eq, hP]
  have hQ : Module.finrank ℝ (LinearMap.ker L) = k := by
    rw [Chapter02.coarea_kernel_finrank hsurj, hT, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin]
    omega
  have hQperp : Module.finrank ℝ (LinearMap.ker L)ᗮ = m := by
    have := (LinearMap.ker L).finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal
    omega
  let C := Chapter02.coareaCoordinates L
  let G : WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) →ₗ[ℝ] WithLp 2 ((LinearMap.ker L)ᗮ × LinearMap.ker L) :=
    C.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap ∘ₗ Φ
  let inl : Rn m →ₗ[ℝ] WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) :=
    (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 ℝ (Rn m × Rn k)).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.inl ℝ (Rn m) (Rn k)
  let inr : Rn k →ₗ[ℝ] WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) :=
    (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 ℝ (Rn m × Rn k)).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.inr ℝ (Rn m) (Rn k)
  let G₁₁ : Rn m →ₗ[ℝ] (LinearMap.ker L)ᗮ := (WithLp.fstL 2 ℝ _ _).toLinearMap ∘ₗ G ∘ₗ inl
  let G₂₂ : Rn k →ₗ[ℝ] LinearMap.ker L := (WithLp.sndL 2 ℝ _ _).toLinearMap ∘ₗ G ∘ₗ inr
  have hC : ∀ t, C t = WithLp.toLp 2 ((LinearMap.ker L)ᗮ.orthogonalProjectionOnto t,
      (LinearMap.ker L).orthogonalProjectionOnto t) := by
    intro t
    simp [C, Chapter02.coareaCoordinates, LinearIsometryEquiv.withLpProdComm_apply]
  have hΨmem : ∀ b, Ψ b ∈ LinearMap.ker L := by
    intro b; rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, hΨ, hL]; rfl
  have h0 : ∀ b, WithLp.fst (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (0, b))) = 0 := by
    intro b
    simp only [G, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, LinearIsometryEquiv.coe_toLinearEquiv]
    rw [← hΨ, hC]
    simp [Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_apply_of_mem_orthogonal
      ((LinearMap.ker L).le_orthogonal_orthogonal (hΨmem b))]
  have hG := Submission.coarea_normDet_block_triangular (Rn m) (Rn k) _ _ G G₁₁ G₂₂ (by simp [hQperp]) (by simp [hQ]) h0
    (fun a => rfl) (fun b => rfl)
  have hGΦ : G.normDet = Φ.normDet := by
    rw [LinearMap.normDet_comp_of_finrank_eq _ _ (by rw [hP, hT])]
    have : (C.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap).normDet = 1 := C.toLinearIsometry.normDet_eq_one
    rw [this, one_mul]
  have hG₂₂ : G₂₂ = Ψ.codRestrict (LinearMap.ker L) hΨmem := by
    refine LinearMap.ext fun b => ?_
    apply Subtype.ext
    simp only [G₂₂, G, inr, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
      LinearIsometryEquiv.coe_toLinearEquiv, LinearMap.codRestrict_apply]
    have : (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 ℝ (Rn m × Rn k)).symm (LinearMap.inr ℝ (Rn m) (Rn k) b) = WithLp.toLp 2 (0, b) := rfl
    rw [this, ← hΨ, hC]
    simp [Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_mem_subspace_eq_self ⟨Ψ b, hΨmem b⟩]
  let lam := Chapter02.coareaHorizontalLinear L
  have hlam : lam ∘ₗ G₁₁ = LinearMap.id := by
    refine LinearMap.ext fun a => ?_
    have h := Chapter02.coareaHorizontalLinear_coordinates L (Φ (WithLp.toLp 2 (a, 0)))
    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.id_apply]
    rw [hL] at h

    rw [← LinearMap.normDet_comp_of_finrank_eq _ _ (by simp [hQperp]), hlam, LinearMap.normDet_id]
  have hlamJ : lam.normDet = (LinearMap.adjoint L).normDet :=
    Chapter02.coareaHorizontalLinear_normDet hsurj

subproblem.title: Vanishing criterion: the co-area Jacobian is zero iff df_x composed with a tangent parametrization is not surjective
subproblem.statement:
Let N, m, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ and x ∈ ℝᴺ, where ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
Let A : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ be a continuous linear map with tangentSpace M x = range A.
Then coareaJacobian M f x = 0 if and only if (fderiv ℝ f x) ∘ A : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ is not surjective.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N m n : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (x : Rn N) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N), tangentSpace M x = LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap → (coareaJacobian M f x = 0 ↔ ¬ Function.Surjective ((fderiv ℝ f x).comp A))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 1–3 of the parent proof (Part (1)), routed through the sibling bridge lemma. This is the route of the parent's parenthetical "apply SimonGMT coareaLinearJacobian_eq_sqrt_det and coareaLinearJacobian_eq_zero_iff to the linear map L".

Notation. Fix N, m, n, M, f, x, A with hT : tangentSpace M x = range A.
- T := tangentSpace M x and D := fderiv ℝ f x.
- L := ((fderiv ℝ f x).comp T.subtypeL).toLinearMap : T → ℝᵐ, so L t = D t for t ∈ T.
- L* := LinearMap.adjoint L : ℝᵐ → T.

1. By the sibling lemma jacobian_normdet_bridge (Submission.coareaJacobian_eq_normDet_adjoint N m M f x), coareaJacobian M f x = normDet(L*).

2. normDet(L*) = 0 iff ker(L*) ≠ 0 (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot: normDet vanishes exactly on non-injective maps). In the parent's terms, normDet(L*)² = det(LL*), and LL* is positive semidefinite with ker(LL*) = ker(L*): if LL*v = 0 then |L*v|² = ⟨LL*v, v⟩ = 0.

3. ker(L*) = (range L)^⊥ (Mathlib LinearMap.orthogonal_range: (range L)ᗮ = ker(L*)). Indeed v ∈ ker L* iff ⟨L*v, t⟩ = ⟨v, L t⟩ = 0 for all t ∈ T. In the finite-dimensional space ℝᵐ, (range L)^⊥ = 0 iff range L = ℝᵐ (Submodule.orthogonal_eq_bot_iff), iff L is surjective (LinearMap.range_eq_top). By steps 1–3, coareaJacobian M f x = 0 ⟺ ¬ Surjective L.

4. Claim: Surjective L ⟺ Surjective (D ∘L A).
   (⇒) Let y ∈ ℝᵐ. Choose t ∈ T with L t = D t = y. Since T = range A (hT), t = A z for some z ∈ ℝⁿ. Then (D ∘L A) z = D(A z) = D t = y.
   (⇐) Let y ∈ ℝᵐ and choose z ∈ ℝⁿ with D(A z) = y. Then A z ∈ range A = T, and the element t := A z of T satisfies L t = D(A z) = y.

5. Negate both sides of step 4 and combine with step 3: coareaJacobian M f x = 0 ⟺ ¬ Surjective L ⟺ ¬ Surjective ((fderiv ℝ f x).comp A). ∎

The case m = 0 needs no separate treatment. Then L* is a map out of the zero space, so normDet(L*) = 1 ≠ 0. Also every map into ℝ⁰ is surjective. Both sides of the equivalence are therefore false, and steps 2–5 cover this case verbatim.

subproblem.statement:
Let N, m, k ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵐ and x ∈ ℝᴺ, where ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
Let P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ) be the Euclidean product, with first component p₁ = WithLp.fst p.
Suppose A : P → ℝᴺ is an injective continuous linear map with tangentSpace M x = range A and (fderiv ℝ f x)(A p) = p₁ for all p ∈ P.
Suppose B : ℝᵏ → ℝᴺ is a continuous linear map with B b = A(toLp(0, b)) for all b ∈ ℝᵏ.
Then coareaJacobian M f x · normDet(A) = normDet(B), where normDet is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet of the underlying linear maps.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N m k : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (x : Rn N) (A : WithLp 2 (Rn m × Rn k) →L[ℝ] Rn N) (B : Rn k →L[ℝ] Rn N), Function.Injective A → tangentSpace M x = LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap → (∀ p, fderiv ℝ f x (A p) = WithLp.fst p) → (∀ b, B b = A (WithLp.toLp 2 (0, b))) → coareaJacobian M f x * A.toLinearMap.normDet = B.toLinearMap.normDet
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Part (2) of the parent proof. Steps 4–5 there pass from A, B to Ã = A|^T and Θ₂ through isometric inclusions, using normDet_codRestrict. Steps 6–9 (the core identity) are the sibling lemma chart_normdet_identity. The identification coareaJacobian = √det(LL*) = normDet(L*) is the sibling lemma jacobian_normdet_bridge.

Notation. Fix N, m, k, M, f, x, A, B.
- T := tangentSpace M x, a finite-dimensional subspace of ℝᴺ with the restricted inner product.
- D := fderiv ℝ f x and P := WithLp 2 (ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ).
- Hypotheses: (HA) A is injective; (HT) T = range A; (HD) D(A p) = p₁ for all p; (HB) B b = A(toLp(0, b)) for all b.

1. A p ∈ T for every p ∈ P, since A p ∈ range A = T by (HT). B b ∈ T for every b ∈ ℝᵏ, since B b = A(toLp(0, b)) ∈ T by (HB).

2. By step 1, define the codomain restrictions (LinearMap.codRestrict) Φ := A.toLinearMap.codRestrict T : P → T and Ψ := B.toLinearMap.codRestrict T : ℝᵏ → T. Thus Φ p is A p viewed in T, and Ψ b is B b viewed in T.

3. Φ is bijective.
   - Injective: if Φ p = Φ q then A p = A q, so p = q by (HA).
   - Surjective: every t ∈ T = range A equals A p for some p, i.e. Φ p = t.

4. Let L := ((fderiv ℝ f x).comp T.subtypeL).toLinearMap : T → ℝᵐ, so L t = D t. By (HD), L(Φ p) = D(A p) = p₁ for all p.

5. Ψ b = Φ(toLp(0, b)) in T for all b: both have underlying vector B b = A(toLp(0, b)) by (HB) (Subtype.ext).

6. Apply the sibling lemma chart_normdet_identity (Submission.coarea_normDet_adjoint_mul_normDet_chart) to m, k, the space T, and L, Φ, Ψ. Its hypotheses are steps 3, 4 and 5. It gives normDet(L*) · normDet(Φ) = normDet(Ψ).

7. By the sibling lemma jacobian_normdet_bridge (Submission.coareaJacobian_eq_normDet_adjoint N m M f x), coareaJacobian M f x = normDet(L*); the L in its statement is exactly the L of step 4.

8. Following a map with the isometric inclusion of a subspace does not change normDet (LinearMap.normDet_codRestrict). So normDet Φ = normDet(A.toLinearMap) and normDet Ψ = normDet(B.toLinearMap).

9. Substituting steps 7 and 8 into step 6 gives coareaJacobian M f x · normDet(A) = normDet(B). ∎

No case distinction is needed: m = 0 and k = 0 are handled inside the two sibling lemmas.
